title: Approval Action API
description: PROPOSED contract, drafted by P3, not yet confirmed by P2. This is what the analyst dashboard (P3) needs to call once a human clicks Approve/Reject on a pending decision in a case's decisions_and_actions[] list (contracts/case_record_schema.json). Today the UI implements this locally as a mock (ui/lib/mock_actions.py, backed by a JSON file) so the approval workflow can be built and demoed before the real agent exists. Swapping the mock for the real endpoint should only require changing ui/lib/mock_actions.record_decision() to call this API instead of writing to the local ledger — no other UI code should need to change, which is why the request/response shapes below mirror decisions_and_actions[] item fields directly. P2: please confirm or amend this before P3 wires it up in Phase 3.

status.description: The human's decision. Matches decisions_and_actions[].status in case_record_schema.json.

actor.description: Who approved/rejected it, e.g. an analyst's name or login. Written to decisions_and_actions[].actor.

note.description: Optional free-text reason from the analyst, e.g. why an action was rejected. Not in case_record_schema.json today — P2 may want to fold this into decisions_and_actions[].decision on rejection, or drop it if unneeded.

review_response.description: 200 OK body — the updated decision, so the UI can render the result without a second read.

status.description: 'executed' if the backend also carries out an auto-executable action immediately after approval, rather than leaving it at 'approved'.

execution_result.description: Optional: what happened when an approved action was executed (e.g. 'card blocked, reissue queued'), if the backend executes synchronously. Null if execution is async or not applicable (e.g. a rejection).

error.description: Human-readable reason, e.g. 'decision already resolved' or 'decision not found'.

review_decision.notes: Idempotency: calling this twice on an already-resolved decision should return a 409-style error_response rather than silently overwriting a prior approve/reject, so two analysts can't race each other. The mock implementation (ui/lib/mock_actions.py) does not currently enforce this — P2's real endpoint should.
